I play a shit ton of games and very rarely post about any of them, but I thought I would post about this one because it is amazing.

CrossCode is a futuristic 16-bit ARPG. The game world is set inside an MMO called CrossWorlds, and it actually kind of feels like an MMO despite it being a single player game. It draws from a lot of different genres and older games, but with a more modern touch. I have even seen a couple of references to other games built into the lore of the world. The setting appears to have drawn from Sword Art Online, yet is unique, I don't think I've ever seen anything like it before.

Visually, it is pretty stunning and varies quite a bit. The gameplay has a few puzzle sections thrown in, but is mostly questing and combat oriented. As far as the storyline goes, I can't say a lot because the game has not revealed a lot so far, but there are multiple different things going on.

The combat so far is:

  • Left click next to your character for melee attack
  • Left click away from your character to range attack
  • Right click to block
  • Right click + WASD to dodge

It sounds pretty simple and it is, but the result is a really fun and fluid combat system that actually makes grinding fun, which almost never happens.

Leveling up and ability upgrades is pretty standard, but they have something similar to the Final Fantasy X sphere system thrown in there for good measure. You can have other people in your party who will fight alongside you, and there are a few different options you can give them for battle tactics. That is, until they go offline, because you're playing an MMO within an ARPG.

Perhaps one of my favourite things about the game is they managed to find an answer to the question: Do we give the player a voice and break the immersion of it being an RPG, or do we make them awkwardly say nothing for the entire game? Instead, there is a bug in the MMO game that you're playing where your character can't say anything, and you unlock various words as you progress.

It reminds me of a game that came out last year just after the first release of CrossCode, called Secrets Of Grindea, except CrossCode feels way more complete, despite its full release being about 6 months away. It is currently in alpha, but it does not seem like it at all. Unless there are parts of the game that I haven't progressed to yet that are unfinished, this game could be a full release as it is.

A review for this game won't do it justice. What makes it so good is the way it blends so many different things into one game, and does it in a way where it doesn't feel odd or forced.

It's 15% off on Steam at the moment.
